One run instead of five: translation → back-check → term check → repair → Medical QA. The order is fixed and it matters: terminology is collected into the glossary by whichever of the two checks finished second; the repair fixes things from the findings of both; Medical QA goes last so that it describes the final text rather than one that will be rewritten a step later.

One model translates, others check — that is the whole point: a check made by the same model that did the translation is not independent.

The server works out the composition and shows all of it: expand a step’s row to see whom it will take and why it will skip the rest. It does not pay twice for a finished check, and it does not let a weaker model overwrite the verdict of a stronger one — there is no need to pick this by hand with ticks any more. The checks are counted for the segments that will be translated in this same run too.

In the same row any step can be started separately and by its own ticks: this is the way to deliberately re-check what the general run considers done.

Ремонт правит только по конкретным наход:
The repair edits only from specific findings and changes as few words as possible — the segment is not translated again, so there is no full run price here. But the previous text will go to “previous translation”, the status will become “needs review”, and the “confirmed by a human” mark will be removed: it referred to a text that no longer exists.

If the score DROPPED after the edit, the text is rolled back together with the previous checks — an unchanged score does not cancel the edit.

For a pass where there was nothing but minor term issues the rule is stricter: it is accepted only if it removed at least one of the issues it was called for. Otherwise it is trading one nitpick for another — work paid for with no movement towards the end.
